incident_name: MV OS 35 Bulk Carrier Collision & Bunker Oil Spill (Gibraltar 2022)

secondary_vessel_involved.name: ADAM LNG
secondary_vessel_involved.role: Moored vessel struck during OS 35 departure

beaching_location.name: Catalan Bay / East Side of Gibraltar

incident_details.spill_nature: Low Sulphur Heavy Fuel Oil (VLSFO), Marine Diesel Oil, and lube oil escaping from ruptured bunker tanks (#1 and #2) after vessel fractured in two
ground_truth_authorities: Government of Gibraltar Department of the Environment
Spanish Maritime Safety Agency (SASEMAR / Salvamento Marítimo)

investigated_sources.data_offered: Monthly/annual raster vessel density maps (hours/km2) derived from commercial feeds (CLS, ORBCOMM, vesseltracker)
investigated_sources.assessment: Explicitly does not distribute raw dynamic AIS time-series

investigated_sources.data_offered: Real-time and historical vessel traffic tracking for EU maritime safety
investigated_sources.access_restriction: Strictly restricted under Directive 2002/59/EC to designated national competent authorities; no public download

investigated_sources.data_offered: Internal radar and AIS VTS operational logs
investigated_sources.access_restriction: Confidential port authority operational data governed by Gibraltar GDPR / Data Protection Act 2004
CEDEX historical database maintained for ministerial and scientific collaboration; no open bulk public download

investigated_sources.data_offered: Aggregated vessel presence and commercial fishing effort
investigated_sources.assessment: Commercial raw merchant vessel trajectories (bulk carriers, tankers, container ships) are expressly withheld due to commercial data licensing
No open continuous multi-vessel dynamic trajectory dataset exists for the Strait of Gibraltar during August-September 2022

ais_evidence_audit.single_vessel_sparse_notes: Discrete collision, beaching, and anchoring positions for OS 35 and ADAM LNG are documented in marine press and casualty reports, but cannot be used for blind multi-vessel candidate generation without causing artificial 1-candidate cheat bias
ais_evidence_audit.commercial_availability: Full continuous multi-vessel terrestrial and satellite AIS for the Strait of Gibraltar is held by Spire Global, MarineTraffic, VesselFinder, and Kpler, accessible only via commercial subscription or institutional license

source_options: HYCOM Global Ocean Physics Analysis GLBy0.08 (expt_93.0)
Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS) IBI (Iberia-Biscay-Ireland) regional model (1/36 deg)
ocean_currents.pipeline_compatibility: Fully compatible with EnvironmentalForcingInterpolator NetCDF reader

source_options: ECMWF ERA5 Reanalysis (0.25 deg hourly 10m u/v winds)
wind.pipeline_compatibility: Fully compatible with EnvironmentalForcingInterpolator CSV/NetCDF reader

comparison_case_004_vs_case_002.sar_temporal_density: Case 004 is superior (4 Sentinel-1 scenes spanning pre-collision baseline, post-beaching, and active spill within 6 days, plus 3 sub-1% cloud Sentinel-2 scenes)
comparison_case_004_vs_case_002.spill_mechanism: Case 002: Long open-ocean approach grounding on coral reef. Case 004: Port departure collision with moored LNG tanker followed by intentional emergency beaching and subsequent structural breakup
comparison_case_004_vs_case_002.hydrodynamic_complexity: Case 004 is substantially more challenging (Strait of Gibraltar two-layer exchange flow, strong tidal oscillations, and lee eddy formation around the Rock)
comparison_case_004_vs_case_002.traffic_density_challenge: Case 004 is an extreme high-density candidate generation test (~300 vessel transits per day through the Strait) compared to moderate open-ocean density off Mauritius
comparison_case_004_vs_case_002.ais_availability_verdict: Identical bottleneck: Both Case 002 and Case 004 have open SAR and environmental forcing, but both are blocked from blind operational candidate generation by the absence of an open, public multi-vessel AIS dataset

feasibility_classification_justification: Case 004 possesses outstanding Sentinel-1 SAR imagery (pre-baseline, post-beaching, and active spill), pristine Sentinel-2 optical imagery, full environmental forcing (HYCOM/CMEMS and ERA5), and unimpeachable official ground truth. However, legitimate public historical multi-vessel AIS for the Strait of Gibraltar is restricted or commercially paywalled. Under the audit decision rules, Case 004 is classified as PARTIALLY_FEASIBLE because SAR and environment are ready, but operational blind multi-vessel candidate generation requires commercial or institutional AIS licensing.
